contributions.statement: When an LLM drafts Gherkin acceptance criteria, measure negative/error-path scenario coverage and spurious-scenario rate separately, because the structured epic-plus-gap-fill pipeline lost negative coverage (81% to 67%) and added spurious scenarios (semantic SSR 10% vs 0%) while looking better on aggregate ratings.
contributions.evidence: Table 2-3; four documents, one model, one run, keyword-matched negative coverage. Audit downgrades the expert-preference and lexical-gap claims to weak.

contributions.statement: Constrain LLM-generated Gherkin with a JSON schema plus a deterministic validator so every scenario is structurally valid before it reaches a .feature file.
contributions.evidence: §4.3 RQ1: 0 invalid of 119 vs 1 invalid for the baseline; validity is guaranteed by construction, so this is a one-scenario margin.

reason: Schema-constrained output is known practice, and the comparison is against a two-sentence prompt with near-zero rater agreement. The loss of error-path scenarios is the only transferable warning, and it is weakly measured.
